steps.description:
Colour sensing is a valuable feature in robotics. A colour sensor detects the colour of a nearby object by measuring the intensity of reflected primary light components, typically red, green, and blue. It then classifies the result into a specific colour name.
The Colour Sensor block gets data from the sensor and outputs the detected colour name.


Our Colour sensor block will classify all colour detected into these 5 colours only:

  • Red
  • Green
  • Blue
  • Orange
  • White

Even if you do not place anything near the sensor, there will still be value in the reading and it will return one of the above colours.


Let's test the sensor by writing a program to repeatedly read the Colour sensor using the Colour Sensor block and display it on the LCD. 

Run the program (either on the physical or virtual robot) and place different coloured objects near the Colour sensor. Does it show the right colour?

The Colour Sensor block returns a text. Hence, you do not need to use Create-text-with block with the LCD. Even if you do, it will still work.
